title: Interaction-driven competing instabilities in two-dimensional checkerboard quadratic band crossing semimetals
authors: Jia-Hao Wen, Wen-Hao Bian, Jing Wang
abstract: Two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals serve as a fertile platform for interaction-driven quantum criticality, nevertheless, the role of the complete fermion-fermion interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this, we systematically investigate the low-energy physics of a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal by considering all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions. Using the momentum-shell renormalization group, we derive the coupled flow equations, which reveal that the low-energy physics is governed by a series of fixed points. Depending on the initial conditions, the system may exhibit a single stable fixed point, several discrete fixed points, or three continuous groups of fixed points parameterized by a few variables. By introducing source terms and evaluating susceptibilities, we identify the dominant and subdominant instabilities. The leading phases include nematic spin-nematic (NSN), quantum anomalous Hall (QAH), chiral superconducting ($\mathrm{SC}_1$), and quantum spin Hall (QSH) orders. Moreover, several features distinguish our findings from previous simplified models. Off-diagonal interactions generate terms that promote orders absent in such models, the continuous groups allow systematic tuning of the leading instability, and trajectory-dependent instabilities emerge where the full RG flow, rather than the fixed point alone, determines the dominant state. These results offer a comprehensive theoretical understanding of low-energy quantum critical behaviors and phase instabilities in two-dimensional QBCP semimetals and related electron systems.
summary: This theoretical work uses the Renormalization Group to study how strong electron-electron interactions drive competing quantum instabilities in 2D semimetals with quadratic band crossings. By analyzing all 16 interaction channels, the authors map out a complex phase diagram, predicting multiple possible ground states like QAH or superconducting orders depending on the system's initial coupling strengths.
main_problem: The paper investigates the role of complete fermion-fermion interactions in driving competing instabilities within two-dimensional quadratic band crossing point (QBCP) semimetals.
main_result: The low-energy physics is highly dependent on initial conditions, leading to various stable phases such as Nematic spin-nematic (NSN), Quantum Anomalous Hall (QAH), and chiral superconducting orders.
method: The primary method employed is the Momentum-shell Renormalization Group (RG) approach, which derives coupled flow equations for all 16 marginally short-range fermion-fermion interactions.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a spin-1/2 checkerboard-lattice QBCP semimetal, analyzed using an effective action combining a quadratic free part and general fermion-fermion interaction terms.
key_observables: Dominant and subdominant instabilities, including NSN, QAH, $\mathrm{SC}_1$, and QSH orders; the evolution of source terms ($\delta S$).
important_parameters: The initial coupling strengths ($\lambda_{ij}$), which determine the flow path between various fixed points (FPs).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that all 16 fermion-fermion interaction channels must be considered, correcting limitations of previous models that used only a subset of interactions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the energy-dependent evolution of couplings, showing how rescaled couplings flow to a fixed point, while Figure 9 and 10 detail one-loop Feynman diagrams for interaction and source term renormalization.
paper_structure: The paper systematically proceeds by introducing the model, deriving the coupled RG flow equations, analyzing the flow trajectories based on initial conditions, identifying the resulting instabilities, and concluding with a comprehensive understanding of the quantum critical behavior.
why_interesting: The detailed RG analysis of competing instabilities and the identification of trajectory-dependent physics provide a rich theoretical framework for understanding emergent topological and correlated phases in low-dimensional materials.
